---
title: "CluMiner — Laboratory quick reference"
---

CluMiner is used in this course for calculations that cannot or should not run
inside GitHub Codespaces. In particular, **CRYSTAL23 runs on CluMiner**.

This page contains only the operations needed by students. Cluster
administration, Slurm configuration and MPI topology are outside the scope of
Mineral Science.

## Connect

Use the access method provided during the course. Once connected, create a
working directory for the activity and keep each laboratory organised.

Example:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/mineral-science/lab02
cd ~/mineral-science/lab02
```

## Transfer an input

Copy the `.d12` input prepared in your Codespace to this directory using the
file-transfer method demonstrated during the laboratory (SFTP/SCP or
MobaXterm).

Confirm that the file is present:

```bash
ls
```

## Submit a CRYSTAL calculation

For Laboratory 2 use exactly:

```bash
cluminer-crystal INPUT.d12 --cores-per-node 2 --threads 2
```

For example:

```bash
cluminer-crystal mgo_shrink2.d12 --cores-per-node 2 --threads 2
```

The resource choice corresponds to:

```text
1 node
2 physical CPU cores
1 MPI rank
2 OpenMP threads
```

Do not request more cores for course calculations unless instructed.

## What the launcher does

The launcher prepares a Slurm job, stages the calculation to node-local scratch,
runs CRYSTAL and returns the persistent results to your working directory.

For an input called:

```text
mgo_shrink2.d12
```

the scientific text output is:

```text
mgo_shrink2.out
```

The calculation itself therefore does not run in your home directory.

## Check the result

After the job has completed:

```bash
ls
```

and check that the expected `.out` file is present.

A valid scientific result must not be assumed simply because an output file
exists. Laboratory 2 checks explicitly for SCF convergence and normal program
termination.

## Transfer the output back

Copy the `.out` file to the corresponding directory in your Codespace:

```text
work/lab02/outputs/
```

The analysis notebook reads the files from there.

## Resource rule for this course

All calculations in the Laboratory 2 convergence series use the same:

```bash
--cores-per-node 2 --threads 2
```

Keeping the hardware request constant makes the timing comparison meaningful
and avoids consuming unnecessary cluster resources.
